quizzes.title: Alphabet Soup
quizzes.description: Crack the letters behind the tech words we use every day.

questions.q: What does "CPU" stand for?
questions.note: The CPU is often called the brain of the computer.

questions.q: RAM stands for Random Access Memory.
questions.note: RAM is short-term memory that is cleared when the power goes off.

questions.q: In web addresses, what does "HTTP" stand for?
questions.note: The extra "S" in HTTPS stands for Secure.

questions.q: What does the "U" in USB stand for?
questions.note: USB is short for Universal Serial Bus.

questions.q: What does "URL" stand for?
questions.note: A URL is simply the address of a page or file on the web.

questions.q: What does "PDF" stand for?
questions.note: Adobe introduced the PDF format in 1993.

questions.q: In email, "CC" stands for "Computer Copy".
questions.note: CC means carbon copy, from the days of typewriters and carbon paper.

questions.q: What does "LED" stand for?
questions.note: LEDs use far less energy than old filament light bulbs.

questions.q: The "www" at the start of web addresses stands for "World Wide ___" what?
questions.note: Tim Berners-Lee came up with the name World Wide Web.

questions.q: What does "SIM" in "SIM card" stand for?
questions.note: The SIM card identifies your phone to the mobile network.

quizzes.title: Tech Titans
quizzes.description: The famous companies behind our gadgets and the people who started them.

questions.q: In which year was Apple founded?
questions.note: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple on 1 April 1976.

questions.q: Google was founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin while they were PhD students at Stanford.
questions.note: Their search engine was first called BackRub.

questions.q: Who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates?
questions.note: Gates and Allen were school friends from Seattle.

questions.q: Which company, founded by Jeff Bezos in 1994, began as an online bookstore?
questions.note: Bezos first named the company Cadabra.

questions.q: Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 from which university?
questions.note: It started as "TheFacebook", open only to Harvard students at first.

questions.q: Samsung is a company from Japan.
questions.note: Samsung is South Korean; it was founded in Daegu in 1938 as a trading company.

questions.q: Which Japanese company created the PlayStation games console?
questions.note: The first PlayStation went on sale in Japan in December 1994.

questions.q: Larry Ellison co-founded which software giant?
questions.note: Oracle was founded in 1977 under the name Software Development Laboratories.

questions.q: Which Finnish company was once the world's biggest mobile phone maker, famous for the 3310?
questions.note: The Nokia 3310 came out in 2000 and is famous for being almost indestructible.

questions.q: A Palo Alto garage called the "birthplace of Silicon Valley" is where which company began in 1939?
questions.note: Bill Hewlett and David Packard started HP there with just a few hundred dollars.

quizzes.title: Web Beginnings
quizzes.description: How the internet and the World Wide Web came to be.

questions.q: Which 1993 web browser first made the web popular with pictures?
questions.note: Mosaic showed images alongside text on the same page; Netscape followed in 1994.

questions.q: At which European research lab did Tim Berners-Lee invent the World Wide Web?
questions.note: CERN sits near Geneva, on the border of Switzerland and France.

questions.q: What was the name of the US military-funded network that became the forerunner of the internet?
questions.note: The first ARPANET message in 1969 was meant to say LOGIN but crashed after LO.

questions.q: Ray Tomlinson was the first person to use the @ symbol in email addresses.
questions.note: Tomlinson sent the first email between two computers on a network in 1971.

questions.q: What was the first .com domain name ever registered?
questions.note: symbolics.com was registered on 15 March 1985 by a computer maker.

questions.q: The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, in 2005, shows what?
questions.note: It's called "Me at the zoo" and stars co-founder Jawed Karim.

questions.q: Wikipedia was launched in 1991.
questions.note: Wikipedia launched on 15 January 2001.

questions.q: What does the "e" in "email" stand for?
questions.note: Email is short for electronic mail.

questions.q: What word for junk email comes from a Monty Python sketch about a café?
questions.note: In the sketch, almost every dish on the menu contains Spam.

questions.q: Stanford students Jerry Yang and David Filo created which famous web directory?
questions.note: It began as "Jerry and David's Guide to the World Wide Web".

quizzes.title: Computing Pioneers
quizzes.description: The machines, minds and milestones that built modern computing.

questions.q: Who is often called the first computer programmer, for her notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine?
questions.note: Her 1843 notes included a method for calculating Bernoulli numbers.

questions.q: What is the name of the test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, of whether a machine can pass as human in conversation?
questions.note: Also accept "the imitation game", Turing's own name for it.

questions.q: Which electronic computer was unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania in 1946?
questions.note: ENIAC weighed around 27 tonnes and filled a large room.

questions.q: A real moth was once found stuck in the Harvard Mark II computer and taped into its logbook.
questions.note: The 1947 log entry reads: "First actual case of bug being found."

questions.q: Which programming language did Guido van Rossum create?
questions.note: It's named after Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake.

questions.q: Which company built Deep Blue, the computer that beat chess champion Garry Kasparov in 1997?
questions.note: It was the first time a computer beat a reigning world champion in a match.

questions.q: Who created the Linux kernel in 1991?
questions.note: He was a 21-year-old student at the University of Helsinki at the time.

questions.q: The C programming language was created at Microsoft.
questions.note: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s.

questions.q: Charles Babbage began designing which mechanical calculating machine in the 1820s?
questions.note: London's Science Museum finally built a working one from his plans in 1991.

questions.q: What was Intel's first commercially available microprocessor, released in 1971?
questions.note: The 4004 was designed for a Japanese calculator company called Busicom.
